title: Museum Puzzle
shortDescription: Match tiles, win jigsaw pieces and restore 100 classic paintings, room by room.
fullDescription:
Restore the paintings, reopen the museum.

Museum Puzzle is a match-3 puzzle game set in an art museum. Swap two tiles to line up three or more of a kind, and reach the level's goal before your moves run out. Every level you win gives you jigsaw pieces of a real painting: drag them into place until the painting is whole and back on the wall. Five paintings restore a room, and twenty rooms reopen the whole museum.

100 paintings in 20 rooms
Every painting in the game is a public-domain work, shown in a photograph that the museum holding it has released for anyone to use. Each room is a period of art, and the rooms go back in time: from the Impressionists through Japanese woodblock prints, the Dutch Golden Age and Persian and Mughal miniatures to portraits of the fifteenth century. Monet's water lilies, Hokusai's Great Wave and Vermeer's Little Street are among them.

A world map of art
Each painting has a pin on an old-style world map, at the place where it was made or the place it shows. Its card gives the title, the artist and the museum that keeps it today. You can look ahead at the rooms to come; their paintings stay covered until you get there.

1,000 levels
• Line up four tiles for a brush that paints a whole line, five for a palette that collects a whole colour, and crossing lines for a paint splash. Swap two of them together for a bigger effect.
• Collect tiles of a colour, break crates, wipe away old varnish, tear the tape off taped tiles and bring frame corners down to the bottom.
• Before a level, pick a brush and a splash, a rainbow palette or extra moves; while you play, use the spatula, the row and column brushes or a shuffle. Every level can be won without boosters.
• Moves left over when you win turn into brushes and pay coins.
• Stop for a few seconds and a hint shows you a move.

Lives, gifts and coins
You have five lives. A life is lost only when you lose a level, and one comes back every 30 minutes. Each day you play brings a booster as a gift, and every painting you complete brings coins and a booster. Coins buy boosters, and five more moves when a level's moves run out.

The shop also sells coins and, once per player, the Apprentice's Bag for real money. Nothing in the shop is random: every pack shows what it holds before you buy it, and every purchase asks you to confirm it first.

Your progress
Your game is kept on your phone and, while Cloud save is on, in your player account as well. Link it to Google Play Games to bring your progress to a new phone. Without a connection, levels play just the same, and your save catches up once you are back online. Delete my data in Settings removes your cloud account and save whenever you like.

The game asks once whether it may send short play statistics, and plays just the same if you say no. It never asks for your name, e-mail address or a password.

The game speaks 13 languages: it starts in your phone's language, and you can switch in Settings.

Every credit, from the museums that hold the paintings to the sources of the painter's figure, is listed in the game under Settings > Support > Credits.
